headline: Sensex Snaps 2-Day Fall, Nifty Reclaims 23,200 Driven by Metals
why: Strong buying in metal and FMCG stocks supported the market recovery ahead of the US Fed meeting.
Positive global cues emerged as Chinese equities rallied on trade talk expectations.
Indices rebounded strongly after snapping a brief two-day losing streak.
whatHappening: Sensex climbed over 330 points while Nifty closed above the 23,200 mark.
Hero Motors IPO saw robust investor response, getting subscribed 4.29 times on Day 3.
A 0.4% fee will be levied on merchants for UPI transactions exceeding ₹2,000.
Bank of Japan raised key interest rates to a 31-year high to combat domestic inflation.

stocksInNews.sources: Apple Pay reported to be eyeing an India rollout in partnership with Axis Bank
Shares rose 2% after Bernstein cited a clearer regulatory path for its ALS drug
Hero Motors IPO reached 4.29x subscription on its final bidding day
Debate intensifies over Tata Sons listing following pushback from Noel Tata

summary: Indian equity markets snapped a two-day losing streak with the Sensex rising 333 points, supported by metals and FMCG sectors. Broader corporate developments included Axis Bank's Apple Pay talks and Zydus Life's drug pipeline boost.
